shortcut_name: reduce the resonance equation to triangle detection
evidence: deepseek uses adjacency and checks `if c in adj[b]`; gpt-oss comments `# edge a-b exists` and computes `common = a_mask & adj[b]`
affordance_in_statement: For each operation, setting S_u[k] = 1 and S_v[k] = 1; and the resonance equation `sum (S_a[k] + S_b[k] + S_c[k])^4 = sum (S_a[k] + S_b[k] + S_c[k]) + 42`.
secondary_shortcut_name: treat operations as edges of a simple graph
removal_suggestion: Make resonance depend on operation order as well as adjacency: if p_ab, p_ac, and p_bc are the input positions of the three pair operations, require p_ab < p_ac < p_bc. The sample outputs already satisfy this, while an arbitrary triangle is no longer sufficient.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the fact that a valid triple is a graph triangle and searches adjacency sets for three mutually adjacent vertices.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The two sequences modified at each position make each input pair an edge, and the fourth-power equation is satisfied exactly when all three pair edges of the triple occur.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses bitmask adjacency and common-neighbor intersection to find the lexicographically first triangle.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The operation list can be represented as an undirected graph, so a resonance is found through an edge and its common neighbors.

common_affordance: The equation collapses to triangle detection because each position has either zero, one, or two selected sequences; only a position with value two contributes 14 to the left-minus-right side, so the required 42 means exactly three pair edges among the triple.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its per-sequence position-set approach effectively enumerates or checks too many triples/position intersections and exceeds the time limit instead of using an efficient graph-triangle method.
It searches for a triangle but does not reliably enforce the required lexicographically smallest triple, so finding an arbitrary valid triangle can produce a wrong answer.

recommended_edit: Add the mutable order-sensitive requirement that, for a resonance (a,b,c), the input positions of pairs (a,b), (a,c), and (b,c) must occur in that order. Keep the existing equation and examples; both sample outputs already meet the new requirement.
